steps.title: Source register and coverage contract
steps.work: Identify the authoritative public sources for every Phase 7–13 population and each required data type before new modeling. Record exact inclusion queries, available fields, coverage dates/counts, access and reuse conditions, refresh limits, alternative sources, and unresolved gaps. Use free public sources first; flag account-required sources for review. Define the bounded archive collections to index, rather than claiming to index every available dataset on the internet.
acceptance: A source register covers planets, Pluto, planetary and small-body moons, NEOs, main-belt and outer bodies, observed long-period comets, satellites/stations/spacecraft, debris, and the inferred Oort model.

Every proposed source has a dated documentation review plus a small access/format probe from the actual acquisition environment; documentation discovery alone does not establish usable access or redistribution rights.

Publish selected-source denominators, unknown totals, exclusions and field/asset coverage. Account-only, inaccessible or legally unclear sources stay unresolved, not silently substituted or counted as acquired.

steps.title: Canonical identities and scientific records
steps.work: Define one stable identity and source-qualified alias system, preserving existing sol, solar:* and HYG IDs through an explicit compatibility map. Separate identities, parent/companion relationships, orbit solutions, physical assertions and asset products. Store units, uncertainties, observation method, source references and conflicts. Preserve measured, estimated, modeled and unknown facts distinctly.
acceptance: Identity fixtures cover renamed/provisionally designated moons, suspected companions, duplicate names, asteroid/comet overlaps, fragments and large satellite catalog numbers.
Merges, splits, redirects and retired records are traceable; never join records solely by name or array position. A provisional designation is not itself evidence that a moon is unconfirmed.

Conflicting source assertions remain inspectable. Select sources per field with documented precedence; do not combine elements from different orbit solutions or infer material composition from a class label.

steps.title: Reproducible acquisition and complete selected imports
steps.work: Build a controlled acquisition process and deterministic importers. Retain immutable raw inputs, source/query manifests, retrieval times, source/parser versions and hashes. Prefer documented bulk snapshots; use bounded, resumable transfers, caching and source-specific throttling. Import the full eligible structured record population in each selected source, not a demonstration handful.
acceptance: Account for every eligible source record as imported, explicitly excluded or unresolved; show duplicates and quarantined malformed records separately. Missing orbit or imagery must not erase an otherwise valid identity.

Detect mixed source revisions and changing pagination with repeatable identity/count checks. If a provider cannot supply a frozen snapshot, disclose the acquisition interval and reconciliation limits; do not claim an instantaneous census.
Repeated builds from retained inputs yield equivalent normalized records. A partial, incompatible or corrupt import cannot replace the accepted release.

Follow current provider policies: serialize JPL SSD API requests, cache results, identify the application and check API versions. Publish cached products to clients instead of embedding JPL API requests in the website.

steps.title: Indexed catalog and searchable review workbench
steps.work: Deliver a working local, read-only catalog browser before new 3D content. Search the complete accepted import by name, stable ID, designation and alias; filter by population, parent, orbit validity/freshness, physical information and asset availability. Use paged results and on-demand dossiers that expose sources and unknowns. Select the storage technology through a bounded comparison, keeping future mobile exports portable.
acceptance: The workbench searches full imported natural and artificial populations and all eligible cataloged moons/companions, including records without renderable positions. Results are not restricted to the visible scene or a preselected sample.

Queries run against indexes with bounded in-memory results and a reusable query contract. Candidate local indexed stores and versioned export chunks are benchmarked before choosing one; no Windows-only binding is imposed on the future phone client.

The asset register is searchable by target, product type, coverage, resolution, rights and readiness. Collection/product IDs, available download URLs and size estimates are recorded; large image/terrain masters remain undownloaded until their body is scheduled.
Identity/alias, parent and field-availability searches have known expected results; a no-result and unknown-data state are distinct from a failed or stale query.

steps.title: Position, time and asset metadata validation
steps.work: Validate the scientific data contract independently of the renderer. Keep source observation/update time, solution epoch, selected display time, center, coordinate frame, time scale, units, method and validity interval separate. Compare representative cases and boundaries for every orbit family with authoritative reference outputs. Audit asset metadata so radar, enhanced color, elevation and natural-color imagery cannot be confused.
acceptance: Freeze source/model-specific numerical tolerances before comparisons. Save reference inputs/outputs for planets, moons, small bodies and artificial objects, including parent offsets, transforms, time conversion and validity-boundary failures.

Support the appropriate propagation model for each source; modern Earth-orbit GP formats and large identifiers are required. Do not treat a two-body estimate, SGP4 and a precise ephemeris as interchangeable accuracy.
Unavailable or stale trajectories remain searchable but are withheld from unsupported precise placement. Predictions are labeled from dated source data, not presented as live tracking.

Asset entries retain product version/LIDVID/DOI when supplied, target, observation date, instrument, projection, registration, vertical datum, units, resolution, footprint, spectral/color interpretation, file size and attribution. Full pixel/terrain validation occurs after download before use, not by metadata inspection alone.

steps.title: Safe updates, storage and offline recovery
steps.work: Stage each new data release, validate it and switch atomically only after acceptance. Retain a last-known-good release, explicit rollback and a change report for renamed, removed, revised and decayed records. Set freshness and offline validity per source/model. Measure storage/transfer costs and a disk reserve before bulk acquisition; separate reproducible catalogs, source masters, caches and code backups.
acceptance: Exercise interrupted transfer, checksum failure, source outage, schema drift, mixed versions, insufficient disk, rollback and offline restart. The accepted catalog remains usable when a refresh fails.

The workbench displays exact catalog release, last successful refresh, orbit validity and local asset availability. Offline cannot falsely imply current observations or an asset that was never downloaded.

Respect current provider refresh rules and cache centrally in the acquisition process. For CelesTrak, check the documented cadence per product; do not retry failures indefinitely or request once per displayed object.

GitHub stores code, schemas, manifests, compact fixtures and evidence. Report actual backup destinations for raw data and large assets; a manifest is not a backup of the referenced binaries. No paid service or new account connection is assumed.

steps.title: Scale acceptance and modeling handoff
steps.work: Measure the workstation baseline and full selected import before accepting readiness. Freeze performance budgets before acceptance runs, publish exact counts and sizes, and keep correctness failures visible. Produce a per-body/family readiness ledger and a reviewable first modeling batch. The user reviews the milestone before Phase 7 asset production and scene placement begin.
acceptance: Measure cold/warm opening, p50/p95 search latency, peak memory, disk/transfer size, rebuild/update time, repeated searches/navigation and offline recovery at the actual full catalog size. Test realistic growth separately; synthetic stress records never count as scientific coverage.

Before acceptance, record numeric budgets and test protocol against the measured hardware, with explicit pass/fail results. This planning document supplies no measured performance pass and does not relax limits to fit a failed run.

Each object/family has independent catalog, trajectory, physical-data, asset-source, downloaded/verified-asset and modeling-readiness states; unknowns and exclusions are visible. Asset source located does not equal asset verified.

The first modeling batch has stable IDs, supported position/orientation data or an explicit data-only state, permitted asset sources or a clearly labeled unknown-appearance treatment, download/storage estimates and review order. Missing maps for an obscure moon do not erase it or block every known planet.

Save the source register, coverage/gap report, reproducible release manifest, searchable workbench, scientific/performance/recovery evidence and handoff in a reviewed GitHub checkpoint. Keep all expansion modeling pending until this gate is accepted.

sources.purpose: Reconcile all cataloged permanent/provisional identities and available physical facts against actual ephemeris coverage. Roster membership alone does not supply a valid current trajectory.

Bulk identity/orbit/classification records, aliases and referenced physical fields where present. Validate full-precision output, pagination consistency and conflicts. MPC bulk access remains to be verified.
Keep confirmed and suspected companions distinct. Optional or incomplete orbit/physical fields must not become invented positions or compositions.

Reference positions and, where supported, rotation/orientation with explicit centers, frames, time scales and coverage. Identify required kernels and their versions; operational and archived mission trajectories differ.

Public orbit records joined to catalog object types. Use modern formats and matching propagation/frame conventions. Space-Track is account-dependent and flagged for review; no credentials or coverage are assumed.

sources.domain: Imagery, spectra, terrain and shape products
sources.purpose: Index selected collections and eligible product metadata for planned targets, including useful maps, calibrated observations, spectra and models. PDS discipline-node coverage must be audited; no single portal is presumed exhaustive. Astropedia acquisition access is unresolved.
Record rights and attribution at dataset/product level, including third-party restrictions. Retain product IDs and references. Source hosting does not itself establish unrestricted reuse.

urls.title: NASA Oort cloud facts and limits

sources.purpose: Keep scientific model assumptions distinct from the catalog of observed comets. No real-ID catalog or exact positions are claimed for unobserved cloud residents.

boundary: This milestone delivers source inventory, reproducible imports, indexed search, data dossiers, numerical proofs and a portable data contract. Phase 7 owns integration into the animated scene, local render origins, GPU/label/picking budgets, Blender assets and installed visual acceptance. Later phases refresh their population audits before integration; mobile stays last.
